data.Unnamed: 1: ‘SHOULD THIS HORSE BE ON ICE?’ — HOW THE % IS CALCULATED

Each timepoint auto-scores the horse's risk of sepsis-associated laminitis, i.e. how strongly prophylactic digital cryotherapy (feet in ice, hoof <10 °C for ~72 h) is indicated. The cell shades progressively green (0%) → yellow (50%) → red (100%). Score = high-risk primary lesion + SIRS criteria:
High-risk primary lesion (Y) — LCV/strangulating GI, colitis, sepsis

Interpretation guide: ≥70% = strong indication, start/continue cryotherapy now; 40–65% = borderline, low threshold to start given how cheap and safe icing is; <40% = lower priority, keep reassessing. Mucous-membrane quality and respiratory rate are additional SIRS signs to weigh manually. Clinical judgment overrides the score.

CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT ONLY — not a substitute for the attending veterinarian's judgment. Confirm all drug doses, fluid rates and thresholds against your hospital formulary and the individual patient before use.

columns: DECISION TRIGGERS — WHEN TO CALL THE ATTENDING SURGEON

data.DECISION TRIGGERS \u2014 WHEN TO CALL TH: Any single red-flag value, or a worsening trend across two consecutive checks, warrants a clinician call. Thresholds are evidence-informed starting points — individualise per patient.

data.Unnamed: 1: Persistent >60 bpm, or rising despite analgesia/fluids
data.Unnamed: 2: Rising HR tracks pain, hypovolaemia and endotoxemia; admission HR is an independent risk factor for post-op mortality.
data.Unnamed: 3: Reassess pain & perfusion; notify surgeon; check PCV/lactate.

data.Unnamed: 1: ≥2 L at any single check, or net reflux on the NGT
data.Unnamed: 2: Post-op reflux after large colon surgery is uncommon but a strong negative prognostic sign (survival ~44% vs ~95% without).
data.Unnamed: 3: Leave/re-pass NGT and decompress; withhold enteral intake; notify surgeon; prokinetic per orders.

data.Unnamed: 1: Rectal T >38.9°C with new colic pain post-op
data.Unnamed: 2: New fever plus colic after intestinal surgery raises concern for a surgical complication (leakage, obstruction, peritonitis).
data.Unnamed: 3: Full exam; consider abdominal ultrasound / abdominocentesis; notify surgeon urgently.

data.Unnamed: 1: Peripheral lactate >4 mmol/L, or failure to clear / rising over serial samples
data.Unnamed: 2: Admission peripheral lactate ≥3.2 and post-correction ≥5 mmol/L are associated with poorer survival; failure to clear signals ongoing hypoperfusion.
data.Unnamed: 3: Bolus balanced crystalloid per orders; reassess CV status; notify surgeon; recheck in 1–2 h.

data.Unnamed: 1: PCV >50% (esp. with TP <4.5 g/dL), or a sharp rise
data.Unnamed: 2: Rising PCV with falling protein indicates plasma loss / haemoconcentration from mucosal injury and endotoxemia; admission PCV is a mortality risk factor.
data.Unnamed: 3: Increase fluid support per orders; consider colloids/plasma; notify surgeon.

data.Unnamed: 1: Bounding digital pulses, increased hoof heat, weight-shifting, or Obel ≥1
data.Unnamed: 2: Sepsis-associated laminitis is a feared sequela of endotoxemic colic; distal-limb cryotherapy reduces incidence and severity in the at-risk window.
data.Unnamed: 3: Confirm/continue continuous digital cryotherapy on both forefeet; foot support; notify surgeon.

data.Unnamed: 1: Score ≥70%, or climbing across consecutive checks
data.Unnamed: 2: A high composite SIRS + high-risk-lesion score marks the developmental window for laminitis, before lameness appears.
data.Unnamed: 3: Start / continue digital cryotherapy (hoof <10°C); confirm plan with surgeon.

data.Unnamed: 1: Pain score ≥2 or escalating analgesia requirement
data.Unnamed: 2: Breakthrough or escalating pain can signal ischaemia, obstruction, or a developing surgical complication.
data.Unnamed: 3: Reassess; analgesia per orders; if unresponsive, notify surgeon for re-evaluation.

data.Unnamed: 1: No manure by 24–48 h, or progressive abdominal distension
data.Unnamed: 2: Delayed transit or distension may indicate ileus, impaction at the anastomosis, or re-displacement.
data.Unnamed: 3: Rectal exam per clinician; withhold/adjust feed; notify surgeon.

data.Unnamed: 1: No urine 6–8 h despite fluids, or rising creatinine
data.Unnamed: 2: Oliguria or azotaemia signals inadequate perfusion or acute kidney injury (NSAID + hypovolaemia risk).
data.Unnamed: 3: Verify fluid delivery & catheter; recheck creatinine; notify surgeon; review NSAID dosing.

data.Unnamed: 1: New heat, swelling, discharge, dehiscence; catheter-site heat/pain
data.Unnamed: 2: Early detection of incisional infection or thrombophlebitis limits morbidity.
data.Unnamed: 3: Clean & document; notify surgeon; consider ultrasound of incision / catheter site.

data.STANDING ORDERS & CARE PLAN (confirm do: Complete the yellow cells for THIS patient. Drug choices below reflect commonly reported post-op large colon management; they are prompts, not prescriptions — the attending veterinarian sets all doses.

data.Unnamed: 1: Balanced solution titrated to perfusion (PCV, lactate, HR, urine). Taper as GI function returns.
Consider synthetic colloid or plasma to support oncotic pressure if TP/albumin low.
Monitor & supplement K⁺, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺; correct deficits that worsen ileus.
Flunixin meglumine commonly used; balance anti-endotoxic/analgesic benefit against renal & GI risk — ensure hydration.
Polymyxin B and/or hyperimmune anti-endotoxin plasma are reported options.
Analgesia + possible prokinetic/anti-inflammatory effect; evidence for reducing reflux is mixed.
Per hospital protocol and stewardship; document drug, dose, route, timing, planned duration.
NSAID + lidocaine ± opioid CRI (e.g. butorphanol); reassess with pain score, escalate/notify if breakthrough.
Decompress and quantify reflux; leave indwelling if reflux ≥2 L or ongoing.
Once reflux resolved, manure passing and comfortable: small frequent handfuls of grass/forage, build up gradually.
Consider if functional ileus (per clinician) once obstruction excluded.
Continuous distal-limb icing of BOTH forefeet while systemically inflamed; keep hoof wall <10 °C for ~72 h; monitor skin.
Use the ‘Should this horse be on ice?’ score — start in the developmental phase, before lameness.
Deep bedding; soft support if indicated; monitor digital pulses & Obel grade each round.
Aseptic catheter handling; inspect incision & catheter site each round; belly band as ordered.
Hand-walk when stable per clinician; monitor demeanor, appetite, attitude.

22,000 IU/kg IM q12–24h. Never IV. Typical 300,000 IU/mL.
6.6 mg/kg IV q24h. Ensure hydration; monitor renal function. 100 mg/mL.
2.2–4.4 mg/kg q12–24h. Reconstituted ~50 mg/mL.
15 mg/kg q8h (up to 25 PO). IV bags ~5 mg/mL.
1.1 mg/kg IV q12h (analgesic). Low anti-endotoxic dose 0.25 mg/kg q6–8h — change rate cell. 50 mg/mL.
0.1 mg/kg q24h maintenance (loading 0.3 mg/kg). Injectable ~20 mg/mL.
0.01–0.02 mg/kg IV prn. 10 mg/mL.
0.2–0.5 mg/kg IV prn (short-acting). 100 mg/mL.
0.005–0.02 mg/kg IV prn. 10 mg/mL.
1,000–6,000 IU/kg IV q8–12h. Nephrotoxic — caution. Reconstitute per label; example 500,000 IU/mL.
0.1–1 g/kg IV as ≤10% solution. 100% DMSO ≈ 1000 mg/mL (1.1 g/mL). Controversial.
4 mg/kg PO q24h (1 mg/kg prevention). Paste conc varies — set conc to compute volume/paste units.

data.WEIGHT-BASED DOSE CALCULATOR \u2014 Post: B.  CONSTANT-RATE INFUSIONS (CRI)  — dose expressed per HOUR

data.Unnamed: 9: Reference & notes
CRI 0.05 mg/kg/min = 3 mg/kg/h after 1.3 mg/kg loading over 5–10 min. 2% = 20 mg/mL. Watch for toxicity.
CRI ~13 µg/kg/h (0.013 mg/kg/h). 10 mg/mL.
0.04 mg/kg/h CRI (0.01–0.1). Watch extrapyramidal signs. 5 mg/mL.
~0.4–0.8 mg/kg/h analgesic CRI (optional). 100 mg/mL.
~0.005–0.01 mg/kg/h (titrate). 10 mg/mL.
Reference & notes
Maintenance 2–4 mL/kg/h; titrate to PCV, lactate, HR, urine. Result = mL/HOUR.
Shock bolus 20 mL/kg, repeat to effect (total up to 40–80 mL/kg). Result = mL per bolus.
4 mL/kg IV once, over 10–15 min; MUST follow with isotonic crystalloids. Result = total mL.

data.EVIDENCE SOURCES: Thresholds are informed by the peer-reviewed sources below. The ‘on ice?’ score combines a high-risk primary lesion with adult-horse SIRS criteria (HR>52 bpm, temp <37/>38.5 °C, WBC >12.5/<5 ×10³/µL, lactate >2.06 mmol/L). Decision support only.
